1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. API: application programming interface; SDK: software development kit

  • Hooks as guardrails that prevent destructive actions
  • Identity validation and authentication, access approval, and authorized access monitoring
  • Managing secrets, credentials and API keys in development and production

2Hooks as Guardrails

Running case

Tidewater's Coding Agent Almost Deletes a Folder

  • An engineer's Claude Code session runs shell commands to clean up files
  • One command would have removed a shared directory
  • The team wants a rule that always holds, even when the model makes a mistake

Hooks run your code at fixed points of the agent loop, outside the model, so they give deterministic guarantees that prompt text cannot.

Hook When Typical guardrail use
PreToolUse Before a tool runs Deny destructive commands (rm -rf, force pushes, writes to .env or production paths), require confirmation, or rewrite arguments
PostToolUse After a tool returns Log for audit, redact secrets from output, normalize results
Prompt submit / stop Around the prompt or the end of a turn Add context, validate the final state
  • A blocking hook can deny a call (a deny decision with a reason, or exit code 2 for command hooks); the model sees the reason and tries something safer.
  • Configure hooks in settings.json (shared project settings for the team, user settings for you) or in the Agent SDK hooks option; use a matcher to target tools such as Bash or Write|Edit.
  • Hooks versus permissions versus prompts: permission rules allow, ask or deny tools by pattern; hooks add custom logic (inspect arguments, call a policy service); prompts only suggest. For destructive-action prevention, use hooks and permission rules.

Exam tip

"The agent must never run X" → a PreToolUse hook or deny rule; "log every tool call" → a PostToolUse hook. Hooks do not make the model wiser: they stop actions.

Exam tip

A keyed browser or mobile app is a leaked key: route calls through your server.

3Identity, Secrets and Key Management

Topic What to know
Identity validation and authentication Verify who is calling: your users authenticate to your application; your application authenticates to Claude with an API key (first-party) or cloud identity (IAM roles on Bedrock, service accounts on Google Cloud)
Access approval and level verification Check what that identity may do before acting; separate roles; require approval for high-privilege actions
Authorized access monitoring Log and review who accessed what; alert on unusual use; track API usage per key and workspace
Secrets management API keys and credentials live in a secrets manager or environment variables, never in source code, prompts, logs or client-side code
Key handling Keys start with sk-ant- and are shown once at creation; store them immediately; set an expiration; use separate keys per environment and service; rotate regularly and revoke on suspicion
Key types Prefer personal or service-account keys (tied to an owner, stop working when the account is removed) over a legacy workspace key
Least privilege Scope keys to the workspace and use cloud IAM roles limited to the allowed models

  • If a key leaks: revoke it, rotate to a new one, remove it from history, and review usage for abuse.
  • Never call the API directly from a browser or mobile app with an embedded key: route requests through your server, which holds the key and enforces the user's permissions.
  • Do not put secrets in prompts or tool results: they can leak through output or injection (Module 13).
  • Use the SDK's environment variable (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) support so keys stay out of code.
Exam tip

Hooks stop actions; they do not make the model's reasoning better. Pair them with permission rules.

4Exam Q&A

S1A coding agent must never execute commands that delete shared directories, even if the model proposes them. Which control fits best?

  • AA PreToolUse hook (or deny rule) that blocks matching commands
  • BA larger context window
  • CA higher temperature
  • DA system prompt sentence saying "avoid deleting things"
Show the answer

Answer: A. A pre-execution hook enforces the rule deterministically; prompts only suggest.

S2A team wants a record of every tool call and its result, with secrets removed. Which hook fits?

  • AA prompt instruction that asks the model to log everything it does
  • BPreToolUse only, because it runs before every single tool call
  • CPostToolUse, to log and redact the output
  • DNo hook can do it
Show the answer

Answer: C. A post-tool hook sees the result and can log and transform it.

S3A developer pastes the production API key into the front-end JavaScript of a customer portal. What is the right fix?

  • ARevoke and rotate the key, and call a server that holds it and enforces permissions
  • BEmail the key to the team so everyone can fix it
  • CKeep it, and only shorten the key a little
  • DObfuscate the key
Show the answer

Answer: A. Keys must never be client-side; a server should call the API on behalf of authenticated users.

S4Where should an API key live for a deployed service?

  • AIn a public wiki
  • BIn the system prompt, so that the model can read it when it needs to
  • CIn a secrets manager or environment variable injected at deploy time
  • DIn source code
Show the answer

Answer: C. Secrets stay out of code and prompts and are injected securely per environment.

S5Which TWO are good key management practices? Select TWO.

  • AShare one key across all teams for simplicity
  • BCommit keys to a private repository
  • CUse separate keys per environment and rotate or revoke them on suspicion
  • DLog keys to help debugging
  • ESet expirations and prefer personal or service-account keys over legacy workspace keys
Show the answer

Answer: C, E. Separation, rotation, expiration and owned keys limit risk; sharing, committing and logging keys do the opposite.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Hooks Run outside the model: PreToolUse (deny, ask, rewrite) · PostToolUse (log, redact)
Block Deny decision with a reason (or exit code 2 for command hooks)
Where settings.json (shared project for the team) or Agent SDK hooks option; matchers like Bash, `Write
Hooks vs prompts Hooks and permission rules enforce; prompts suggest
Keys sk-ant-…; shown once; secrets manager or env var; expire, separate, rotate, revoke
Never In code, prompts, logs, git or client-side code
Identity Users authenticate to your app; app authenticates to Claude (API key or cloud IAM)
Monitoring Log and review access; track usage per key and workspace
